Hardness under prescribed counts neither entails nor contradicts unrestricted-count existence.

originality.rationale: The source-dated 2024 Hajebi--Javadi paper treats prescribed counts and parameterized complexity, without this universal mixed-size biclique degree-sum threshold. Harangi treats uniform stars in random regular graphs. The full relevant 2026 Lee paper gives a different multipartite bound at k=3 but no all-k biclique threshold. Older pure-star and mixed path/star results differ. Searches of the available semantic index and primary literature found no equivalent statement, but unindexed early design literature is a priority risk.
residual_risks: Older unindexed or inaccessible star-design articles might imply the same biclique threshold under another formulation; no independent exhaustive literature review.
Cameron--Horsley and historic Tarsi/Yamamoto criteria potentially have specialized corollaries not independently checked in all old appendices.
The November 17, 2026 directly related Lee preprint presents complementary results and future developments could affect historical priority.

value.rationale: A sharp natural infinite-family threshold with a concrete infinite obstruction and explicit existence mechanism. The result includes highly unbalanced bicliques that generic expansion conditions do not handle, and identifies the numerical-semigroup conductor as the exact all-k boundary. No claim of broader graph classes or prescribed-count feasibility.
